instruction.text: Are these statements true or false? Choose the correct answer.

atoms.a: A triangle always has at least one line of symmetry.

end.text: This is a scalene triangle. It doesn’t have any lines of symmetry.

atoms.a: A circle has an infinite number of lines of symmetry.

text: As long as a line passes through the centre of a circle, it will be a line of symmetry.

atoms.a: This rectangle has four sides, so it must have four lines of symmetry.

text: That rule only works for regular polygons. This is not a regular polygon because the sides aren’t the same length. A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry.

atoms.a: This parallelogram has no lines of symmetry.

end.text: This parallelogram does not have any lines of symmetry.

atoms.a: This star has five lines of symmetry.

text: You could draw a line of symmetry from each point of the star to the opposite side.

atoms.a: This kite has twice as many lines of symmetry as this trapezium.

text: This kite and this trapezium both have one line of symmetry.

atoms.a: This arrow only has one line of symmetry, which is diagonal.

text: This arrow only has a diagonal line of symmetry.
